tools.name: scrubjay
tools.description: Scan a training or eval dataset for live-shaped API keys and personal data before it leaves your machine, and get back a pseudonymised copy that still trains plus an encrypted mapping only you can reverse. It exists because every hosted scanner has the same absurdity at its heart: uploading the file to learn whether the file is safe to upload IS the disclosure. 27 recognisers on by default out of 29 — 4 checksum-validated (Luhn, IBAN mod-97, ABA 3-7-1, SSN structural exclusion), 19 published provider prefixes, 4 structural, and 2 heuristics that ship SWITCHED OFF because a scanner that cries wolf gets turned off and a scanner that gets turned off protects nobody. Three decisions carry the build. (1) TWO SPANS PER FINDING, always: overlap resolution uses the whole match, redaction uses the capture group, and they differ on five rules — redacting match[0] on url-embedded-credential destroys the scheme, user and host of a DSN, and a pem-private-key rule that matches only the header redacts 30 characters and leaves the entire key body in the file you are calling clean, which is the worst failure this product can have (a test asserts that span exceeds 78 chars). (2) IT NEVER PARSES YOUR JSON: JSON.parse -> JSON.stringify turns 12345678901234567890 into ...67000, 1.0 into 1, and drops duplicate keys, while TextDecoder substitutes U+FFFD over the invalid UTF-8 that real multi-GB exports contain — so detection decodes a COPY and the splice works on the original bytes, with spliceBytes(raw, []) returning the same object. (3) GZIP GOES THROUGH FFLATE, NOT DecompressionStream, at a measured 2.26x cost, because `cat shard-00.gz shard-01.gz` is routine in sharded pipelines, browser multi-member behaviour is unverified, and the gzip ISIZE check is UNSOUND on it (equal shards make a truncated read pass) — silently scanning half a file and reporting clean is the worst outcome available. The entropy heuristic was redesigned after measurement killed the obvious version: H >= 3.5 bits/char flags English prose (4.53) and git SHAs (3.91) while MISSING real 20-char hex secrets (mean 3.36), because max entropy at length L is log2(L) and a constant bits/char gate is length-coupled by construction; what ships is length-normalised eta = H/log2(alphabet) at 0.92, behind an unbounded candidate tokeniser and ten structural suppressors — and it is still off by default. Pseudonyms are HMAC-SHA256 folded to 50 bits in Crockford base32; the sketched PERSON_0f3a (16 bits) was unshippable at a 50% collision point of 301 values. Triage is keyboard-first on ONE verb: unreviewed means redacted, so triage only lets you un-redact what it got wrong. Honest limits are stated first, not buried: no personal names and no postal addresses (GLiNER cut at 192 MB), a checksum rules out a typo not a coincidence (~1 in 10 random nine-digit strings passes ABA, asserted in the suite because the UI prints it), US SSNs have had no checksum since 2011 so an order number like 192-83-7465 does match, and a clean report means nothing matched rather than that the file is clean. Two real bugs were caught by the browser dry-run rather than by unit tests: a self-referential `await writeChain` inside a .then() on writeChain that deadlocked every run at 100%, and an idempotence break where the unquoted branch of generic-secret-assignment re-matched its own [REDACTED:...] marker because ] sits outside its character class.
browser_apis: File.stream() + ReadableStream — multi-GB streaming with no upload; .getReader() and a while loop, NEVER `for await...of` a ReadableStream (async stream iteration is Safari 27, i.e. essentially no iPhone in the field)
Web Workers (module) + MessageChannel — a reader worker owns the bytes end to end and talks to N scanner workers over private ports, so the main thread never touches the hot path

Transferable ArrayBuffer with COUNT-based credits — the credits ARE the backpressure, so the reader physically cannot allocate ahead of the pool; resident memory is exactly workers x 2 x chunkBytes (64 MiB desktop, 6 MiB mobile) at any file size. Credits are a count rather than a recycled buffer because in pass 2 the splicer returns the SAME buffer when a chunk is clean, so it cannot simultaneously be the output and the credit. No SharedArrayBuffer, hence no COOP/COEP, hence it runs on GitHub Pages unmodified

Web Crypto HMAC-SHA256 — stable pseudonyms (same email always the same token) folded to 50 bits of Crockford base32, memoised per worker because a non-extractable CryptoKey means one subtle.sign per distinct value

Web Crypto PBKDF2 (600,000 rounds, the current OWASP figure) + AES-GCM-256 — the mapping container, with an explicit key commitment because AES-GCM is not key-committing (Albertini et al., USENIX 2022). The wrong-passphrase and altered-header cases are DELIBERATELY reported with one combined message, because prk = f(passphrase, salt, iterations) means the commitment shadows the AAD for exactly the header fields AAD protects — a test asserts the combined string verbatim so nobody 'fixes' it into a false promise

First-party position-preserving JSON string scanner (unit-tested) — walks raw bytes and returns each string literal with an RFC 6901 pointer plus a decoded-index -> byte-offset map, so a value like "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIEow\u002FABC" (10 decoded chars over 15 raw bytes) splices at the right byte

First-party byte splicer (unit-tested) — spliceBytes(raw, []) returns the same object with zero copies; overlapping and out-of-range edits throw rather than corrupting output; invalid UTF-8, big integers, 1.0, 1e5 and duplicate keys all survive byte-identically

First-party recogniser registry (29 rules, every pattern carrying the `d` flag, asserted by test) with two independent spans per finding and a published does-not-match line per rule rendered in the preflight UI

First-party validators (unit-tested): Luhn, IBAN mod-97 with a SWIFT length table, ABA 3-7-1, three-valued SSN structural exclusion (never a boolean — a `=== true` caller silently dropped every known-invalid plant during design), and jwtDecodable implemented against atob NOT Buffer.from, because Buffer is lenient and would accept 'eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9!!!' in Node while the browser throws

First-party length-normalised entropy gate with ten structural suppressors (hex-digest case-insensitively incl. 48, uuid, iso8601, semver, media-b64 magic prefixes, path, single-class, wordy, plus scrubjay's own pseudonym and redaction-marker forms for idempotence) — candidate extraction is UNBOUNDED at the top end because a {24,512} cap splits a 1400-char base64 blob into pieces and the 376-char tail then fires

First-party overlap resolver (unit-tested) — lower tier wins, spans are half-open so adjacent findings both survive, suppressed findings are RETAINED because the triage kill-count and the context projection both need them, and a rule-name tiebreak makes output a deterministic function of input (which is what makes a golden-file test possible)

First-party context projection — the 40-char window is computed from the FULLY redacted text with post-redaction offsets and every candidate span applied, so a dismissed high-entropy blob next to a reported email cannot walk into findings.csv in plaintext; surrogate pairs are clamped explicitly because String.prototype.at is not code-point aware

First-party RFC 4180 CSV writer — control chars become visible escapes so one finding is always one physical line (deliberate deviation: a findings.csv whose row count differs from its line count cannot be wc -l'd or grep'd), `;` triggers quoting for de/fr/es Excel locales, leading =/+/-/@ gets a formula-injection prefix, UTF-8 BOM, CRLF, and JSON pointers have PII-shaped object keys masked because the path column leaks on its own
fflate Gunzip — multi-member-correct gzip input, chosen over DecompressionStream at a measured 2.26x cost because the ISIZE trailer check is unsound on concatenated members
CompressionStream('gzip') — optional gzip output, defaulted OFF because compression runs at roughly a twelfth of read speed

hyparquet 1.27.1 + hyparquet-compressors — Parquet read one row group at a time in 262 KB of pure JS instead of a 150 MB DuckDB bundle; the largest row group is computed from the footer and printed BEFORE the scan, because 'nothing lands in memory' is false on that path

File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker + createWritable, where the awaited write IS the backpressure) — mode:'exclusive' deliberately unused because it is Chrome 121+ only and writes in place, so a tab crash leaves a truncated file that looks complete. Falls back to an in-memory Blob hard-capped at 512 MiB, then findings-only, with the branch and its ceiling stated in preflight

Crockford base32 project key (unit-tested exhaustively over 1,260 single-character substitutions: zero silently produced a DIFFERENT key; the handful that validate are documented O/0 and I/L/1 folds decoding to the identical key, which a 20-bit checksum cannot reject by construction)

Rejection-sampled passphrase (9 words from a 390-word list = 77.5 bits; 6 words would be 51.6 and is not enough against a GPU at 600k PBKDF2 rounds), with NO auto-copy to clipboard because Universal Clipboard and Windows Cloud Clipboard sync it between devices
Four-way overlay dismissal on every modal and the drawer (x control, backdrop pointerdown, Escape, outside-panel pointer), verified at 375px with real touch-type PointerEvents rather than .click()
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; installable, offline app shell + precached sample)

tools.name: searchpack
tools.description: Point it at a folder of docs and it builds a semantic search engine on your own machine — a binary index, a subsetted embedding table and a dependency-free search.js, zipped. Unpack it into your site's public/ and you have search: no account, no vector database, no per-query cost, nothing hosted. The engine then runs on your READERS' machines, so nobody's queries reach anyone, including you. The idea that makes it possible: sentence-transformers/static-retrieval-mrl-en-v1 is not really a neural network — its entire ONNX graph is Gather(table, ids) -> DequantizeLinear -> ReduceMean, so an embedding is the average of one uint8 table row per word piece. Searchpack therefore skips ONNX Runtime completely: a ~200-line protobuf reader lifts the uint8[30522,1024] table out by name, and the averaging happens in plain JS. That is the only reason a search engine can be handed to a third party at all — 26 KB of JS instead of 11 MB of WASM. The per-tensor scale (1.2497) factors out of the mean and is annihilated by L2 normalisation, so only zero_point=121 is needed. Three findings from adversarial review changed the build. (1) sentence-transformers calls encode_batch(add_special_tokens=False), so adding [CLS]/[SEP] 'to match the reference' is the DEVIATION — it moves a one-word query by cosine 0.24. (2) Subsetting the TOKENIZER vocabulary is the obvious optimisation and is wrong: WordPiece is greedy longest-match, so removing entries re-segments unknown words rather than silencing them — 41% of held-out words become in-index pieces, and a search for 'carpet' would confidently retrieve every page about CARS. So all 30,522 token strings ship (~230 KB) and only the ~1,000 embedding rows the corpus touches are subsetted, applied as a post-filter. (3) Plain mean-pooling is dominated by function words: 'how do I stop it retrying forever' scored 0.03 and ranked an unrelated page first; IDF-weighted pooling using document frequencies computed from the user's OWN corpus takes it to 0.46 and ranks correctly, at one float per shipped row. Retrieval is three modes in the shipped shim — semantic (256-bit binary-code Hamming pre-pass via counting sort, then exact int8 cosine rescore), Okapi BM25 over the same word pieces, and reciprocal-rank-fusion hybrid (the default, because pooled embeddings are weakest on exactly what docs search gets most: identifiers, flags, error codes). The pack verifies itself before download: the EMITTED search.js is loaded from a Blob URL and run against the EMITTED binaries — round-trip cosine 1.000000 across 20 chunks, exact because the tokenizer and engine are literally the same source files in both places (?raw imports of src/shim/*.runtime.js); binary pre-pass kept 100% of exhaustive results; a failing pack is still emitted, labelled 'unverified'. HTML extraction is first-party rather than Readability precisely because Readability discards the heading ids a docs search needs to deep-link. Honest limit stated in the UI, not buried: static embeddings score ~35 on MTEB Retrieval vs ~43 for all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and ~52 for bge-small; measured on the bundled 18-page sample, five conversational questions phrased to avoid the answering page's wording put the right page in the top three TWICE. English only. Nothing you select ever leaves the tab; the sole network call is one anonymous pinned GET of the public model, cached for offline use. Generated packs are released under MIT (not AGPL) so users can ship them on their own sites.
browser_apis: First-party ONNX protobuf reader (~200 lines, no ONNX Runtime, no WASM): walks ModelProto -> graph -> initializers AND node-attribute subgraphs, locating embedding.weight_quantized BY NAME rather than by hardcoded offset; reads scale from float_data (field 4) and zero_point from int32_data (field 5), NOT raw_data — a raw_data-only reader silently returns garbage (measured cosine 0.0046 vs 0.9999); hard-rejects a QInt8 re-export rather than mis-decoding it, and explains itself when weights live in an external .onnx_data file

First-party WordPiece tokenizer verified byte-for-byte against HuggingFace on 39 committed fixture cases: BertNormalizer (clean_text -> handle_chinese_chars -> strip accents -> lowercase, in that order because strip_accents:null follows lowercase and runs BEFORE it) + BertPreTokenizer + greedy longest-match with whole-word [UNK] collapse. Two real bugs it caught: JavaScript's \s matches U+FEFF but Rust's is_whitespace does not, so format characters must be filtered BEFORE the whitespace fold or a BOM splits a word; and max_input_chars_per_word is counted in CODE POINTS, so 60 astral emoji (120 UTF-16 units) must not trip the 100-character gate

The shared-runtime trick: src/shim/*.runtime.js are plain dependency-free JS with hand-written .d.ts siblings; the app imports them normally and the packer imports the SAME FILES with Vite's ?raw suffix and concatenates their literal source into the emitted search.js — so build-time embedder and shipped shim agree BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by discipline (round-trip cosine measured at exactly 1.000000)

First-party IDF-weighted pooling (unit-tested): embedding = normalize(SUM idf(t) * (row[t] - zeroPoint)), with idf computed from the user's own corpus in a first tokenization pass, floored so a ubiquitous token contributes a trace rather than vanishing; also gives a principled 'no signal' test — a nonsense query whose summed weight falls below a floor returns nothing instead of ten arbitrary neighbours (nonsense does NOT become [UNK]: bert-base-uncased has every letter, so 'zzqqxwv' shatters into ubiquitous single-character subwords)

First-party binary formats (unit-tested round-trip incl. alignment): vocab.bin = all token strings + u16 rowIndex filter + f32 IDF weights + the subsetted uint8 rows; index.bin = 256-bit binary codes + int8 vectors + f32 norms + BM25 postings + metadata JSON, with every typed-array view kept 4-byte aligned by explicit padding

First-party two-stage semantic retrieval: Hamming distance over 32x-smaller binary codes selected by a COUNTING SORT over the distance range (no comparison sort), then exact int8 cosine rescore of candidates only; int8 quantisation scale cancels because the stored int8 norm is the divisor

First-party Okapi BM25 (k1=1.2, b=0.75) over the same word pieces, with the inverted index built at load time from forward postings, fused with the semantic ranking by parameter-free reciprocal rank fusion (RRF, k=60) so a cosine and a BM25 score need no comparable scale

Self-verifying artefact: dynamic import() of a Blob URL loads the EMITTED search.js and drives the EMITTED binaries — parity, binary-pass recall vs exhaustive, self-retrieval hit rate, and 8 adversarial queries (empty, single-word, accented, CJK, 400-char token, nonsense); requires blob: in the CSP script-src

fetch + CORS to huggingface.co, pinned to an immutable revision SHA — one anonymous GET of onnx/model_int8.onnx (31,259,319 B) and 0_StaticEmbedding/tokenizer.json (711,396 B); note the tokenizer is in a SUBFOLDER, the repo root 404s

Cache API — the table is stored after the first run so every later build is fully offline (disclosed honestly: on iOS Safari, storage for a site unvisited for 7 days is cleared unless installed to the Home Screen)
Web Worker (module) — download, parse, chunk, embed, pack and verify off the main thread with determinate byte- and chunk-level progress; the live playground queries the pack in the worker

DOMParser structural HTML extraction (main thread — workers have no DOMParser): strips nav/header/footer/aside/[role=navigation]/sidebar/TOC and KEEPS heading id attributes, which is exactly what Readability discards and precisely what a docs search needs to deep-link to page.html#section
File System Access API (showDirectoryPicker + showSaveFilePicker) with DataTransferItem.webkitGetAsEntry recursion, <input webkitdirectory> and .zip drop as first-class fallbacks
fflate — reads .zip input and writes the search.zip artefact; CompressionStream does gzip/deflate only and cannot write a ZIP container

Matryoshka (MRL) truncation done on the ROWS before summing, which is exactly truncate-then-normalise and therefore matches encode(truncate_dim=256, normalize_embeddings=True) rather than the non-unit vectors normalize-then-truncate would give
Web Share API (level 2, files) + Clipboard API + localStorage (settings only, never document content)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; installable, offline app shell + sample precached)

tools.name: chatprint
tools.description: See the literal string your model actually receives. Paste the request body your code was about to send and chatprint renders it through the model's OWN Jinja chat template, tokenizes it with the model's OWN tokenizer, and attributes every token to a segment — system prompt, tool definitions, retrieved documents, each turn, template overhead — then packs it down to a budget. It exists because the two things that eat a context window (tool definitions and retrieved documents) are precisely the two you never see. The headline finding is measured, not asserted: the same 20-message sample costs 6,478 tokens on Granite 3.3, 6,237 on Qwen2.5, 6,119 on Llama 3.1 and 1,900 on Phi-3.5 — because four of the ten templates tested SILENTLY IGNORE the tools array, so those models would never know the tools exist. The second is that Llama 3.2's own template injects the current date near the start of the prompt, so the identical request rendered a day later shares only a 24-token prefix out of 6,119: its template destroys 99.6% of your prompt cache every day with no help from your code. Attribution is the hard part and is done by LOCATING rather than counting: tokenizing messages separately is out by +23/-60 on a 53-token prompt, and subtracting consecutive prefix counts is also wrong because Phi-3.5 appends eos_token when add_generation_prompt is false. Instead every cut point is found by longest-common-TOKEN-prefix against the one ground-truth token array, so spans tile [0,total) and the column sums to the truth by construction. Two guards came from real bugs caught during the build: prefixes must be rendered WITH the tools (Llama splices them into the first USER message, and rendering prefixes without them collapsed every cut onto the final turn while still summing exactly), and a separate degeneracy check hides a breakdown where one segment holds >90% of tokens — because the sum invariant cannot catch that class of failure. Also caught: encode() applies the post-processor and adds a SECOND beginning-of-text token on Llama and Mistral because the template already wrote one, so every count uses add_special_tokens:false. Artefacts: rendered-prompt.txt (byte-exact), token-budget.csv (one column per model compared) and messages.trimmed.json (packed to fit, never orphaning a tool result from its call, never silently dropping the system prompt, always keeping the final turn). Honesty is enforced in the UI: Claude is labelled ESTIMATE inline and never default-selected because no public local tokenizer exists after Claude 3, with Anthropic's free count_tokens endpoint named as the exact alternative; OpenAI rows are labelled as OpenAI's documented per-message accounting rather than a byte-exact render; gated repos (meta-llama, google/gemma, all Cohere) are absent because they 401 anonymously, and faithful community mirrors are badged 'mirror'. Nothing you paste leaves the tab — the only network request is an anonymous GET of a public tokenizer file, listed in the event log. Installable PWA, offline after the first tokenizer download.
browser_apis: @huggingface/jinja 0.5.9 — renders the model's real chat_template; jinja PRE-DECLARES strftime_now/raise_exception/range/namespace, so passing them in the context throws 'Variable already declared' and kills every render — they are injected through a hand-built Environment instead, which also pins the clock so a render is byte-reproducible (the thing that makes the cache-diff demo possible)

@huggingface/tokenizers 0.1.3 — exact token ids in PURE JavaScript: no WASM, no native binary, zero transitive dependencies, ~8.7 kB gzipped; two-argument constructor (tokenizer.json AND tokenizer_config.json) or it throws 'Config must be a valid object'

add_special_tokens:false on every encode — the chat template already writes <|begin_of_text|>/<s> into the string, and the post-processor otherwise adds a SECOND one (measured: 4 ids for '<|begin_of_text|>Hello world' where the model sees 3)

First-party token-LCP cut-point attribution (unit-tested): cut points found by longest-common-token-prefix against the ground-truth token array, so segment spans tile [0,total) exactly and the displayed column sums to the truth by construction; self-corrects for prefix renders that diverge from the real prompt

First-party degeneracy guard: a collapsed attribution still sums exactly, so a separate check flags >90% of tokens in one segment and refuses to draw the breakdown while still showing the (correct) total

First-party tool-span location by brace-matching the serialised schema in the rendered text — ablation reports 'tools: 0' on Qwen (spliced into the system block) and mis-attributes on Llama (spliced into the first USER message)

First-party packer (unit-tested): welds an assistant tool_call to the tool results answering it so neither is orphaned, protects the system prompt and the final user turn, and validates the packed conversation before export
First-party prompt-cache prefix diff with six named cache-breaker diagnoses tied to documented provider invalidation rules, and an explicit statement that TTL expiry is undetectable from a token diff

First-party loss-mask analyser: {% generation %} sentinel path (sentinels embedded RAW inside single quotes — JSON.stringify makes jinja throw 'Unexpected escaped character: u') with a verified-equivalent universal path, plus four anomaly checks including the classic untrained end-of-turn token that makes a fine-tune never stop generating
gpt-tokenizer 3.4.0 — real OpenAI vocabularies, dynamically imported and split per encoding (o200k 1.02 MB gzip, cl100k 436 kB) and excluded from the service-worker precache, which stays at 307 KiB

fetch + CORS to huggingface.co — anonymous GETs of tokenizer_config.json / tokenizer.json / config.json; CORS present on every hop including the signed CDN redirect, no preflight; 401 GatedRepo bodies are PLAIN TEXT so status is checked before .json()
Cache API — a tokenizer (1.8 MB to 31.8 MB, measured; the idea's claimed 0.7–2.2 MB was wrong) downloads once and the tool then works offline
config.text_config.max_position_embeddings fallback — Gemma 3's multimodal config nests the context window, which is why other tools report it unknown
chat_template.jinja sidecar fallback — SmolLM3 and gpt-oss keep the template beside tokenizer_config.json rather than inside it
Web Worker (module) — download, parse, render, encode and attribute off the main thread, with determinate progress and an event-log sink forwarded to the main thread
First-party multi-dialect parser: OpenAI body, Anthropic body (top-level system string, input_schema tools, tool_use/tool_result content blocks) or a bare messages array
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker with anchor-download fallback) + Clipboard API + Web Share API (level 2)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; installable, offline app shell + sample precached)

tools.name: ggufscope
tools.description: Will this GGUF fit on your GPU? Paste a Hugging Face repo id (or drop a local .gguf) and GGUFScope reads the model's REAL tensor table straight out of the file with a single HTTP Range request — about 8 MB of a multi-gigabyte model, ~0.1% of it — then computes exactly what it needs in VRAM. It exists because the SEO 'VRAM calculator' pages guess from a parameter count and a quant name, and both inputs are unreliable: Q4_K_M is a llama-quantize MIXTURE (attention V, the FFN down projection and the output head are stored at higher precision, and a row length not divisible by the block size silently falls back to another type — qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf is 133 Q5_0 tensors and only 12 Q4_K, a true 6.16 bpw vs the assumed 4.85), and the KV cache depends on GQA geometry a parameter count cannot reveal (Qwen3-32B declares key_length 128 while 5120/64 = 80, an 8192 vs 5120 MiB error at 32k that says a model fits when it does not). Weight bytes come from ggml's real block sizes; the KV cache reproduces llama.cpp's own per-layer formula including explicit key_length/value_length, per-layer head_count_kv and the 256-token context padding. The killer assertion is a self-check: the summed tensor table is reconciled against the file's true size read from Content-Range — exact match shows 'verified', a mismatch is surfaced rather than hidden, which catches fork quantisations, removed ggml types and truncated downloads for free (delta 0 bytes on every model tested). Solvers find the largest -ngl and the largest context that fit. Sharded models are fully supported (shards 2+ are ~10 KB each). Artefacts: fit-report.json, a solved llama-server command line (which forces -fa on whenever the KV cache is quantised, because llama.cpp exits otherwise), an Ollama Modelfile, chat_template.jinja rendered live, and a 1200x630 report-card PNG. A local .gguf is read with Blob.slice and never uploaded; remote inspection is honestly disclosed as a request to Hugging Face. Working memory is shown as an adjustable allowance, never folded silently into the headline, because llama.cpp's compute buffer has no closed form; MLA and sliding-window models are flagged as upper bounds. KV figures are checked in CI against numbers llama.cpp itself printed at startup.
browser_apis: fetch + HTTP Range requests (the headline: Range is a CORS-safelisted request header, so a single bytes=0-N request fires no preflight; huggingface.co 302s to its CDN which answers 206)
CORS Access-Control-Expose-Headers: * → the browser can read Content-Range and learn a 20 GB file's true size without downloading it (x-linked-size is only on the 302 hop, which fetch hides)
Guard against a server that ignores Range and answers 200: the body is stream-read to the requested length and then cancelled, so the tool never downloads the model it exists to avoid downloading
Blob.slice (the identical parser over a local file, header only, never uploaded — fully offline)

First-party GGUF binary parser (DataView + TextDecoder, little- and big-endian): magic/version/counts, the full metadata KV block, and the tensor-info table; throws NeedMoreBytes on a truncated prefix rather than yielding zero-shaped tensors, which is the failure mode that would silently report 0 GB

Progressive Range ladder (8 MB → 24 MB → 64 MB → 160 MB): the tensor table sits AFTER all metadata, and the tokenizer vocabulary is in that metadata, so real headers start 5.7–7.5 MB in (measured: Qwen3-8B 5.68 MB, Llama-3.2-1B 7.47 MB, gemma-3-4b 6.24 MB, Qwen3-32B 5.70 MB) — one request covers the overwhelming majority
Huge string arrays are WALKED, not materialised: the 128k–260k-entry tokenizer vocab is skipped by length prefix, with only the BOS/EOS/PAD/UNK entries decoded by index for the chat-template preview

First-party ggml type table (unit-tested): block and type sizes for every type F32…MXFP4/NVFP4/Q1_0/Q2_0, verified twice over — by compiling ggml-common.h and printing sizeof for every block struct, and by diffing llama.cpp's gguf-py/gguf/constants.py; removed types (Q4_2, Q4_0_4_4, IQ4_NL_8_8…) have a zero block size and are hard-rejected instead of dividing by zero, and ids beyond the upstream enum are refused as fork quantisations

First-party VRAM arithmetic (unit-tested against llama.cpp's own startup logs): weights as Σ align(elements/blockSize × typeSize, alignment); KV cache as Σ_layers n_ctx × (key_length × head_count_kv × bytes_k + value_length × head_count_kv × bytes_v) — Llama-3.1-8B at 131072 f16 gives 16384.00 MiB, matching the figure in its own log, and TinyLlama/Llama-3.2-1B/Qwen3-32B all match at f16 and q8_0

First-party reconciliation self-check: dataStart + Σ aligned tensor bytes vs the real Content-Length — 'verified' at delta 0, and a named diagnosis (header-only fixture / truncated download / fork quantisation) otherwise

First-party offload model: -ngl offloads the LAST N blocks (llama.cpp's i_gpu_start), the output head only when ngl > n_layer, the token embedding stays on the host; plus binary-search solvers for the largest fitting -ngl and the largest fitting context on a 256-token boundary

Hugging Face tree API over CORS (paginated via the Link: rel=next header, limit caps at 1000) to list a repo's .gguf files with real LFS sizes, and to group split models so a 49 GB eight-way shard set is offered as one entry
Web Worker (module) + AbortController — fetch and parse off the main thread with determinate progress; superseded requests are cancelled

@huggingface/jinja (the only runtime dependency) — renders the model's own tokenizer.chat_template against example messages, with a failure shown as the thrown error plus the template source rather than a wrong count
Canvas 2D — the 1200x630 shareable fit-report card, rendered on-device
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker for JSON/PNG/.jinja, anchor-download fallback) + Web Share API (level 2, files) + Clipboard API (the command line and Modelfile)
localStorage (GPU size, context, cache type preferences only; never model data)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; installable, offline app shell + the synthetic sample header precached)

tools.name: tiltwell
tools.description: A spirit level, angle finder, inclinometer and roof-pitch meter in your browser — it turns the phone's orientation sensor into a precise 2-axis bubble level and a clinometer, then hands you the number as a saved measurement, a CSV and a report card. Lay the phone flat to check a shelf is level; hold it against a slope to read the angle, percent grade, roof pitch (rise-in-12) and 1:n ratio, with an accessibility-ramp reference (1:20 / 1:14 / 1:12); Calibrate zeros it against a reference surface.
